C-KERNEL-EFFECT-FENCE-REVOCATION-2026090.Summary: Add a generic effect-fence contract so revocation, cancellation, runtime replacement, and activation-epoch changes prevent already admitted work from committing new privileged effects.
C-KERNEL-EFFECT-FENCE-REVOCATION-2026090.Problem: The current broker authorizes at admission and revokes handles and runtime authority, but the Astra audit found no general guarantee that an in-flight operation rechecks authority at the actual effect sink. A caller can therefore be admitted, lose authority, and still commit a later state, browser, filesystem, network, or credential effect unless every provider independently closes that race.

Goals.Goal: Define an opaque host-issued effect fence bound to invocation, principal, runtime, installation, grant lineage, resource target, and activation epoch.
Define a trusted sink-side linearization point that orders revocation against commit authorization without a validation-to-effect race.
Make cancellation, grant revocation, runtime death, replacement, and activation change invalidate future commits from stale work.
Preserve truthful Incomplete outcomes when an external effect may already have escaped before invalidation.
Provide a reusable sink-admission contract for later browser, network, filesystem, credential, and UI brokers.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL DOES NOT APPROVE A PLAN OR IMPLEMENTATION.
C-VNEXT-ARCHITECTURE-DECISION-20260906 must be applied before this change is planned.
Authorization at invocation admission remains necessary but is not sufficient for effect commit.
EVENT BUS IS NOT RPC and event delivery cannot validate, approve, cancel, or complete an effect.
The generic kernel mechanism must not contain browser, filesystem, network, credential, UI, or provider-specific policy.
Revocation cannot claim to undo a remote effect that was already dispatched; such outcomes remain Succeeded, Failed, or Incomplete according to evidence.
A check followed by an independently scheduled effect is insufficient: revocation and commit authorization must be serialized by the authoritative effect owner.
If a provider cannot atomically order its commit with host revocation, it cannot be the authority boundary and must dispatch through a broker that can.
Trace and correlation identifiers are evidence only and confer no authority.
The approved browser-search spec and plan remain unchanged.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Durable package catalog or revision switching.
Implementing browser, network, filesystem, credential, or UI policy.
Universal distributed transactions across remote services.
Automatic retry of Incomplete external effects.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A versioned generic EffectFence or equivalent opaque contract is issued only by trusted host authority and cannot be forged or widened by a provider.
The fence binds the exact runtime, installation, invocation, resource scope, operation, grant lineage, and activation epoch required by the selected sink.
For an owned local effect, fence validation and commit authorization share one atomic transaction, lock, compare-and-commit operation, or equivalent linearizable mechanism at the authoritative sink.

For an external effect, consuming the one-shot dispatch authorization is the linearization point: invalidation ordered first prevents dispatch, while dispatch ordered first remains Succeeded, Failed, or Incomplete according to evidence.
A deterministic race matrix pauses before and after the linearization point and proves both legal orderings without a window in which stale authority can initiate a new effect.
A replacement race proves the old runtime cannot receive commit authorization after a new activation epoch is selected.
A cancellation race never reports Denied for an effect whose dispatch or commit already linearized, and never reports success for an effect whose invalidation linearized first.
An external-effect fixture distinguishes invalidation before dispatch from Incomplete after uncertain dispatch and never retries the latter automatically.
Effect-fence metadata and denial telemetry exclude raw payload, credentials, page content, and persisted values.
Existing ProviderSelf, delegation attenuation, bounded RPC, state leases, and event/RPC separation remain compatible.
Architecture checks prevent domain-specific target types from entering the generic fence implementation.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh deterministic race evidence shows that revoke, cancel, crash, replacement, and epoch changes stop future privileged commits while already dispatched external effects remain truthfully classified.

Assumptions.Assumption: Current invocation, grant, lifecycle, and state-lease identities can supply a compact host-side fence without exposing authority-bearing internals across IPC.
Each later privileged broker can identify and own a linearization point at which it atomically orders domain validation and commit or dispatch authorization.
Compatibility can be introduced additively before older providers are removed.
